intents.title: M-x compile
intents.desc: Build the compile command from the language of the code_*.html focused last, and send cd and then the compile command to the xterm.html focused last. Nothing is sent to Emacs -- it runs locally from resolver.dispatch's browser.backend branch (lib/vent/compile-intent.js).
intents.notes: The target panels are resolved from cursor.html's focusHistory (role: code / xterm), so it works the same in any skin and in separate windows. The cd target is decided by compile.json's scope (file/self/root).

intents.title: Agenda
intents.desc: Open or focus the Agenda (the task list a task_table cut, panels/tool/list.html?config=agenda; D-task-list). Nothing more. Changing a state or making a task is done with that panel's own keys (t / d / x / M-n) -- there is no operation on tasks that are not on screen.
intents.notes: The tasks are rows of a note's markdown table (Table: <name>), edited in a task_table and cut into the task list (~work/books/task_list.json) -- not org-mode's syntax or files; only the vocabulary (TODO/DONE, C-c a) follows Emacs org-mode.

intents.title: M-x nix compile
intents.desc: The same as compile.run, but an environment wrapper (default nix develop --command) is put in front of the built command before it is sent.
intents.notes: prefix is an extra field only lib/vent/compile-intent.js reads (not resolver.js). The prefix is put in front of the argv, which is then made into one shell line (argv joining, not a string template, so the command's quoting needs no second thought).
